baby.1: ✦In the first week, the baby hasn't actually implanted in your womb yet.✦Pregnancy lasts 40 weeks, but it is counted from the first day of your last period, not from implantation.✦During the first week, an egg cell starts to develop in your left or right ovary.
baby.2: ✦Before your baby starts growing, you set the stage.✦Last week's rise in estrogen and progestin in your blood prompted your womb to build a rich, blood-filled lining ready for a possible fertilized egg.✦At the same time, eggs are maturing in fluid-filled sacs in your ovaries called follicles.
baby.3: ✦At the start of this week (usually around day 14 of a 28-day cycle) you ovulated.✦One of your eggs left its follicle and travelled to the fallopian tube.✦Over the next 12–24 hours, one of the roughly 250 million sperm released by your partner will swim through the vagina, pass the cervix, enter the womb and try to reach and enter the egg in the fallopian tube.✦If it succeeds, the egg will be fertilized.✦About 400 sperm survive this journey, and only one manages to break through the egg's membrane.
baby.4: ✦Over the next 30 hours, the nuclei of the sperm and the egg will join to combine their genetic material.✦If the sperm carries a Y chromosome, your baby will be a boy; if it carries an X chromosome, you'll have a girl.
baby.5: ✦On its 3–4 day journey from the fallopian tube to the womb, the fertilized egg – the zygote – divides into 16 identical cells.✦Once it reaches the womb, the zygote is called a morula.✦One or two days later it settles into the lining of your womb and continues its amazing development and transformation.
baby.6: ✦At this stage your developing baby is just a tiny ball of cells, scientifically called a blastocyst.✦The blastocyst has an inner cell mass that will form the embryo and an outer cell mass that will form the placenta; there is also a fluid-filled cavity that will become the amniotic sac.✦The outer cell mass becomes the placenta, the organ that brings oxygen and nutrients to your baby and carries waste away.
baby.7: ✦Your last period started 12 to 16 days ago.✦So you're probably ovulating now or will ovulate soon.✦Although pregnancy really lasts about 38 weeks, the exact moment egg and sperm meet can't be known, so doctors calculate the due date as 40 weeks from the start of your last period.✦That's why you're already counted as 2 weeks pregnant when fertilization happens.✦Timing really matters if you want to conceive.✦To improve your chances, have intercourse between 72 hours before and 24 hours after ovulation.✦This lines up the sperm's 72-hour lifespan with the egg's 24-hour lifespan.✦Your partner should keep this window free too.✦To ease the pressure on both of you, it helps to know how long conception usually takes.✦Most couples only announce a pregnancy after several tries.✦If you're trying to conceive and still drink, smoke or take medicines, now is the time to stop.✦Your body should be in the best possible shape for the baby.✦Talk to your doctor about starting folic acid and vitamin supplements to lower the risk of birth defects.
baby.8: ✦In the second week of pregnancy (around day 14 of a 28-day cycle) the released egg is pushed into the fallopian tube.✦Within the next 12 to 24 hours, out of about 250 million sperm making the tough 10-hour journey through the vagina, cervix and uterus to the fallopian tube, around 400 survive and only one enters the egg's membrane.✦The surge in LH peaks within 24 to 36 hours; this process, commonly known as ovulation, ends with the mature egg being fertilized by the right sperm.
baby.9: ✦When the due date is calculated, counting starts before fertilization – from week 2 – even though sperm and egg haven't met yet.✦Women have about a 25% chance of getting pregnant in each menstrual cycle.
baby.10: ✦After its 3–4 day journey from the fallopian tube to the uterus, the fertilized egg is now called a zygote and divides into 16 identical cells.✦When the zygote enters the uterus it's called a morula.✦Growing at an astonishing pace over 1–2 days, the morula burrows into the uterine wall and settles there.
baby.11: ✦By now your developing baby has become a small ball of cells, called a blastocyst at this stage.✦This cluster of cells is the embryo itself.✦The sac filled with amniotic fluid is connected to the placenta.✦The placenta is the organ that carries the oxygen and nutrients your baby needs to live.
baby.12: ✦Changes continue in both the baby and the mother-to-be in the first weeks of pregnancy.✦The baby keeps growing during these weeks.✦The endometrium – the lining of the womb – starts to thicken.✦This thickening allows the embryo formed after fertilization to attach securely to the womb.✦Blood flow to this area increases to meet the needs of your newly developing baby.
baby.13: ✦Once the embryo settles in your womb, the little ball of cells splits in two.✦One part will form the embryo and the other the placenta.✦The placenta is an organ that forms during pregnancy, feeds your baby around the clock and leaves the womb together with the baby once its job is done.✦Your metabolism, changing with pregnancy hormones, and your womb are already working together to build the system that will carry oxygen and nutrients to the new embryo and placenta.
baby.14: ✦Sperm, scientifically called spermatozoa, are the male reproductive cells.✦Sperm production in the testes begins at puberty.✦Each sperm cell has 3 parts.✦These are the head, the midpiece and the tail.✦A healthy man releases 150–200 million sperm during intercourse.✦But only about 1,000 sperm manage to get close to the egg.✦Of these, the fastest and most active sperm succeeds in fertilizing the egg.✦The egg must also be ready for fertilization to happen.
baby.15: ✦A lot is happening in your belly right now.✦Your baby is a ball of cells growing at a furious pace.✦This ball of cells is called a blastocyst.
baby.16: ✦Once the blastocyst implants in the womb, the part that will form the placenta begins producing the pregnancy hormone hCG.✦This hormone tells your ovaries to stop releasing eggs.✦It also triggers high production of estrogen and progesterone.
baby.17: ✦The hCG hormone is what makes a pregnancy test turn positive.✦A pregnancy test taken at the end of this week will be positive.✦(If the test is negative and your period hasn't come, try again in a few days.)
baby.18: ✦In the cavity that will become the amniotic sac, amniotic fluid starts collecting around the blastocyst.✦This fluid will cushion and protect your baby in the coming weeks and months.
baby.19: ✦Right now your tiny blastocyst gets oxygen and nutrients and removes waste through a simple circulation of microscopic channels connected to the small blood vessels in your womb.✦Next week the placenta will take over this job.
baby.20: ✦A few days after the important meeting of sperm and egg in your body, the fertilized egg is no longer just one cell.✦Your baby is still very small, but the number of cells grows by the hour.✦This cluster of cells, also called the zygote, travels down the fallopian tube toward the womb this week.✦The journey takes about 6 days; when the zygote reaches the womb, it takes up the position where it will grow for 9 months.✦As the cells keep multiplying, some become the embryo and some form the placenta.✦Then production of hCG, known as the pregnancy hormone, begins.✦Thanks to this hormone your body stops producing eggs and increases estrogen and progesterone.✦Meanwhile, amniotic fluid fills the space around the zygote, forming the amniotic sac that will cushion it for months.✦Until the placenta develops enough to do its job, your baby gets oxygen and nutrients – and removes waste – through a simple circulation of microscopic channels connected to the vessels in the uterine wall.
baby.21: ✦Although you won't know for a while, your 3-week-old baby's sex is already decided.✦Your fertilized egg has 46 chromosomes – 23 from the mother and 23 from the father. Of the two types, X and Y, the X chromosome always comes from the mother.✦The chromosome from the father can be either X or Y.✦If the baby has XX chromosomes, you'll hold a girl in your arms in 9 months; if XY, a boy.
baby.22: ✦This week of pregnancy signals the start of the embryonic period.✦From now until week 10, all of your baby's organs – and even some of their functions – begin to develop.✦This makes it the period when your baby's development is most vulnerable to any disruption.✦Right now the baby is an embryo about the size of a poppy seed.✦This poppy-seed-sized embryo (about 3 mm) contains layers called the epiblast and hypoblast.
baby.23: ✦While you're still wondering whether you're pregnant, your baby has already found its place.✦The blastocyst has completed its journey from the fallopian tube to the womb.✦The burrows it makes in the lining of the womb create connections that will last through the last 8 months of pregnancy (and, in a way, a lifetime).✦Very soon the tiny cells settled in the womb divide into two groups.✦One group will become the embryo itself, while the other shapes the channels the baby will use to receive nutrients and remove waste throughout life in the womb.
baby.24: ✦Although the embryo is smaller than 1 mm, its development is very intense.✦As the amniotic sac forms around the embryo, the yolk sac is also forming.✦The yolk sac will later help start up the baby's developing digestive system.✦The embryo now has three distinct layers of cells, each growing into specific parts of the baby's body.✦The innermost layer, the endoderm, gives rise to the digestive system, liver and lungs.✦The middle layer, the mesoderm, forms the heart, sex organs, bones, kidneys and muscles.✦The outermost layer, the ectoderm, forms the nervous system, hair, skin and eyes.
baby.25: ✦This week marks the beginning of the embryonic period.✦From today until your tenth week, all your baby's organs will start to develop, and some will even start working.
baby.26: ✦Your embryo is the size of a poppy seed and at its most sensitive to anything that could threaten its development.
baby.27: ✦Your placenta is forming; by the end of this week it will start passing nutrients from your blood to your baby.
baby.28: ✦Meanwhile, the amniotic sac your baby is growing in is producing red blood cells.✦This way it nourishes your baby until the placenta takes over.
baby.29: ✦Your baby is now about the size of a sesame seed.✦Your baby keeps growing fast.
baby.30: ✦At this stage the embryo is made of layers called the ectoderm, mesoderm and endoderm.✦The ectoderm is the layer where the brain, spinal cord, nerves and spine develop.✦The ectoderm also forms the skin, hair, nails, tooth enamel, and milk and sweat glands.
baby.31: ✦The second layer, the mesoderm, is where the heart and circulatory system form.✦It also forms muscles, cartilage, bones and the tissue under the skin.
baby.32: ✦The endoderm layer shapes the lungs, intestines, urinary system, thyroid, kidneys and pancreas.✦From this week, the placenta and umbilical cord start doing their job.
baby.33: ✦This week, in the inner layer called the endoderm, cells that will form the endocrine glands, digestive system and bladder begin to take shape.✦As the circulatory system begins to form, the baby's tiny heart starts beating, though you can't hear it yet.✦You'll be able to hear your baby's heartbeat at an ultrasound around weeks 10 to 12.
baby.34: ✦Can the baby be seen this week? A 5-week gestational sac can only be seen with a transvaginal ultrasound.✦But it's normal not to see the baby or the heartbeat inside the sac yet.✦That's simply because the baby is still too small to be seen.
baby.35: ✦Sex in the fifth week of pregnancy is completely harmless.✦In a normal pregnancy there are no restrictions on your sex life until the last 4 weeks.✦But you may not always feel like it.✦In the first trimester, including this week, hormonal swings, nausea and tiredness can dull your desire.✦This usually changes in the second trimester.
baby.36: ✦This week your baby's mouth, ears and nose have started to take shape.
baby.37: ✦If you could look inside your womb, you'd see a head with small dark spots on it.✦Those are your baby's eyes and nostrils.✦The two little hollows on the sides of the head are the ears.
baby.38: ✦The arms and legs have started to form.✦The heart beats 100–160 times a minute.✦Blood has started to flow around the body.
baby.39: ✦The intestines are developing, and the bud that will later become the lungs has appeared.✦The pituitary gland and the rest of the brain, the bones and muscles are taking shape.
baby.40: ✦This week your baby is the size of a lentil, but by the end of the week will be three times bigger.✦The nose, mouth and ears you won't be able to stop looking at in 8 months start to form this week.✦If you could look inside your womb, you'd see the head with dark spots where the eyes are forming.✦The developing ears are already making small bumps on the sides of the head.
baby.41: ✦The hard part of being 6 weeks pregnant is, of course, that you haven't told anyone yet.✦Your baby's heart now beats with a regular rhythm and blood has started circulating.✦Until birth, your baby's heart will beat about 150 times a minute – twice an adult's rate – some 54 million times in total. The intestines are developing and the tissue that will form the lungs has appeared. The brain, muscles and bones are forming along with the pituitary gland.
baby.42: ✦This week, blood from the mother reaches the baby via the placenta through the umbilical cord.✦The placenta produces hormones that support the baby's development and sends nutrients and oxygen.✦The placenta also helps remove waste from the baby's body.✦Thanks to the filter between mother and baby, they can have different blood types.
baby.43: ✦At 7 weeks your baby is about 10–13 mm long – roughly the size of a bean or a small grape.✦It weighs about 2 grams.
baby.44: ✦This week there's a noticeable jump in your baby's growth rate.✦Your baby grows 2–3 times bigger than last week.
baby.45: ✦This week the baby's face keeps developing more clearly.✦A tiny mouth and tongue start to form.✦Leg buds begin to appear.✦The arm buds from last week grow larger and take on a paddle shape.✦The hands and shoulders begin to form.
baby.46: ✦This week the eyes, nostrils, gallbladder, intestines and pancreas continue to develop more clearly.✦The structures of the ears begin to form.✦The eyelids are almost complete.
baby.47: ✦At seven weeks the joints of the knees, elbows and wrists have formed.✦Other organs continue to develop at the cellular level.✦The baby's sex has been determined at the cellular level.
baby.48: ✦This week the thyroid gland keeps developing.✦The central neural tube separates into the brain and spinal cord.✦The baby's brain grows bigger.✦Nerve cells begin to form that will carry messages from the brain to the body.✦The delicate, interconnected forebrain, midbrain and hindbrain have begun to form.
baby.49: ✦At 7 weeks the right and left heart valves start to develop.✦The heart beats much faster than last week.✦It beats about 180 times a minute – twice an adult's rate.✦Blood circulation has begun.✦The digestive system starts to form as small buds.
baby.50: ✦This week the hands and feet are forming tiny webbed fingers and toes.✦Your baby's tail begins to disappear.
baby.51: ✦In about a month, when there's more room in your baby's belly, the intestines will move from the cord back into the abdomen.
baby.52: ✦As the intestines form and there isn't enough room in the abdomen, a loop moves into the umbilical cord.✦Even at this early stage the intestines carry waste out of the body.
baby.53: ✦Your baby is growing like a storm.✦This week the length has passed 1 cm – at 8 weeks your baby is about 1.4 to 2 cm long.
baby.54: ✦Whoever you choose – obstetrician, family doctor, nurse practitioner or midwife – it's very important to trust their approach and care.✦Visits are usually scheduled once a month, becoming more frequent in the last two months until your baby arrives.✦These regular check-ups are perfect chances to ask questions and share your worries, so come prepared!
baby.55: ✦The tips of your baby's milk teeth are forming.✦Bone cells have started to shape and tiny joints are developing.✦The webbing between the fingers and toes is getting thinner.
baby.56: ✦Your baby is moving inside your belly, but you can't feel it yet.
baby.57: ✦Your baby is now about 2 cm long.✦The eyelids are forming and the ears are developing.✦The tooth roots in the gums continue to take shape.
baby.58: ✦Your baby's hands have now separated into 10 tiny fingers.✦Even though you can't feel it yet, your baby is becoming more active.✦They can move their arms and legs, turn their head and open and close their mouth.
baby.59: ✦Taste buds are starting to form in the mouth and on the tongue.✦While the eyes develop in detail, the nose has become recognizable.✦Your baby's major organs – brain, heart, lungs and kidneys – continue to develop.
baby.60: ✦It's still too early to see the sex on an ultrasound, but small movements can be seen.✦Muscles and bones keep developing.✦At this stage, it's important to support the developing body with vitamin D (ask your doctor).
baby.61: ✦Your baby's eyes are still on the sides of the head; in the coming weeks they'll move toward the middle.✦One exciting milestone is near: this week the eyelids are getting ready to open and close!
baby.62: ✦Your baby can open and close their mouth and turn their head.✦They can move their arms and legs.✦The mother-to-be won't feel these movements yet.
baby.63: ✦Almost all of the baby's organs have started working.✦The digestive system has begun to form.✦The liver is starting to work and the pancreas has started producing insulin.✦The intestines have started moving into their place in the abdomen.✦The four chambers of the heart, beating 160–180 times a minute – twice your rate – formed last week.✦The valves that keep blood flowing through the heart have formed.
baby.64: ✦This week your baby has reached about 3 cm.✦At this stage the brain is developing much faster than other parts.✦The head looks large compared with the rest of the body.
baby.65: ✦Your baby can bend their arms, which helps the muscles develop.✦They can wiggle their newly separated little toes.
baby.66: ✦If you could see inside, you'd see the spine beneath the transparent skin.✦During this period your baby becomes more active during the day.✦Their activity can be described as sleeping and waking states.
baby.67: ✦Along with the developing jawbone, tiny tooth buds are forming.✦Bone and cartilage are developing in the body, and tiny ear canals in the head.
baby.68: ✦This means you've passed a critical period in your baby's development.✦You can take a breath of relief now.✦Most congenital abnormalities appear before 10 weeks of pregnancy.
baby.69: ✦This week, 250,000 neurons are produced every minute.✦That means the brain is developing faster than ever.✦The kidneys produce more urine, and if your baby is a boy, the testes produce testosterone, the male hormone.
baby.70: ✦During this period your baby becomes more active during the day.✦Their activity can be described as sleeping and waking states.
baby.71: ✦Last week your baby entered the fetal stage.✦From now until birth the baby will be called a fetus.✦As the fetus grows this week, the heart rate slows down.✦The heart starts beating more slowly, below 160 beats a minute.
baby.72: ✦The chest and belly slowly start to flatten.✦Organs, including the intestines, keep developing.✦The baby practices breathing by inhaling small amounts of amniotic fluid.✦The skin has become thicker.✦Signs of hair begin under the surface of the skin.
baby.73: ✦As the sense of touch keeps developing, the baby can now respond reflexively to outside stimuli.✦For example, if the mother presses her belly with her hand, the baby may move away by reflex.✦The baby doesn't feel any pain yet.
baby.74: ✦This week the sense of taste also starts to develop.✦All of this shows that the first learning is beginning in the brain.✦Pay even more attention to what you eat and drink.✦Avoid drinks containing substances like caffeine and alcohol, which can stay in your baby's blood for up to 100 hours.
baby.75: ✦The yolk sac, which produces blood cells, keeps shrinking and will disappear over the next few weeks.✦Your baby's vocal cords have also started to form.
baby.76: ✦The lenses of the eyes and the eyelids have formed.✦The eyelids are still closed.✦The facial bones are clearly visible.✦The bones continue to harden.✦The chin becomes more defined.✦The first tooth buds in the jawbone keep developing.
baby.77: ✦At 11 weeks the baby's genitals start to change shape: a clitoris forms in girls and a penis in boys.✦Many mothers-to-be wonder whether the sex can be seen at 11 weeks.✦But it's still too early to guess the baby's sex.
baby.78: ✦Nails have appeared.✦The tiny nail beds have started making nails – get the baby nail clippers ready.✦Most babies are born with long nails that need trimming soon after birth.
baby.79: ✦The truly critical period of your baby's development is coming to an end.✦By the end of this week every body part will be in place; even the genitals will have developed (though it's still too early to tell the sex).
baby.80: ✦Lights out.✦This week the eyelids have formed and will close.✦They'll stay fused until the end of the second trimester.
baby.81: ✦Feed me! Put away the takeaway menus: your appetite is back!✦Around this week many women say they can feel 'the baby is hungry'.✦Make sure you eat enough and keep a healthy diet, but don't think you need to 'eat for two'.
baby.82: ✦What's normal and what isn't? As your blood volume increases to nourish your baby, your gums may feel sensitive and bleed when you brush or floss.✦Although it's uncomfortable, it's completely normal.
baby.83: ✦This week your baby is about 5–6 cm long, the size of a plum.✦It weighs about 13–14 grams.
baby.84: ✦Here's some exciting news while your little one grows: your baby can do acrobatics in the womb.✦This week your baby can climb, turn upside down, stretch backwards and even do somersaults inside your womb.✦They can kick with those tiny legs.✦And practically box with their arms.✦They're probably having a great time in there.
baby.85: ✦This week your baby is about 7–8 cm long, about the size of a lemon or tangerine.✦It weighs about 22–25 grams.
baby.86: ✦This week your baby's face is still small in proportion to the body.✦They look cuter with each passing day.✦The facial features have become more defined.✦The forehead is broad.✦As the ears grow, they take on their normal shape.✦The inner and middle ear have fully formed.✦The eyes have moved further toward the front of the face.✦The eyes have gained colour.
baby.87: ✦The baby's skin is covered with fine hair.✦Your baby can put their thumb in their mouth.✦By this week all of your baby's organs and body systems have formed.✦The organs keep growing and developing, and the arms and legs keep getting longer.
baby.88: ✦The baby's digestive system is working well.✦The baby swallows amniotic fluid, filters it through the kidneys and intestines and releases it back into the amniotic fluid as urine.✦All waste is passed through the umbilical cord to the placenta and from there into the mother's blood.
baby.89: ✦All of your baby's tooth buds keep developing.✦Your baby can now stretch the whole body and respond to outside stimuli with reflex movements.✦Babies don't feel any pain from these stimuli.
baby.90: ✦The heart is a little slower than in previous weeks, but still beats fast.✦The yolk sac disappears completely this week.✦The intestines are now fully settled inside the abdomen.
baby.91: ✦Your baby's head is half the length of the body, but the body will catch up in the coming weeks.✦The developing organs have started working.✦The liver secretes bile, the pancreas produces insulin and the kidneys make urine.✦The vocal cords have also started to develop as your baby prepares to communicate after birth.
baby.92: ✦This week your baby is 8–9 cm long, about the size of a medium apple.✦It weighs about 43–45 grams.
baby.93: ✦In boys the prostate is forming; in girls the ovaries are moving down toward the pelvis.✦This week lanugo – temporary fine hair that falls out within a few weeks after birth – has appeared on the skin.✦It's thought to keep the baby warm until enough fat builds up under the skin.
baby.94: ✦This week the baby's brain keeps developing.✦The connections between brain, nerves and muscles are nearly complete.✦As nerve fibres are now covered with a fatty myelin layer, messages from the brain start reaching organs and muscles.✦This shows in the facial muscles too.✦Over the past weeks the baby started making various (uncontrolled) facial expressions; this week they go further – frowning or making a sour face.
baby.95: ✦This week the placenta keeps growing and producing hormones for the baby's development.✦Until birth it provides the nutrients and oxygen the baby needs.✦The placenta also works as a filter.✦It helps reduce the effect of some factors, such as medicines the mother has to take.
baby.96: ✦An ever-growing uterus.✦At each prenatal visit your provider will note the size of your uterus by measuring from your pubic bone to the top of the uterus (fundus).✦In general this measurement matches the week of pregnancy you're in.
baby.97: ✦On ultrasound this week your baby still looks roomy and comfortable.✦In the images the baby's head is often on the right with a hand near the chest.
baby.98: ✦There are only a few weeks left until you can learn your baby's sex.✦Your doctor might see it this week or give you a hint.✦Since a guess could be wrong, you can ask your doctor not to tell you anything yet if they're not sure.
baby.99: ✦Your baby is 10–11 cm long, about the size of a medium peach.✦It weighs about 70 grams.
baby.100: ✦Your baby's eyes are still tightly closed and won't open until about week 23.✦But they can now notice bright light coming through your belly and hear sounds.
baby.101: ✦The thyroid hormones have been working for a few weeks.✦Last week a fatty layer called myelin began forming around the nerves connecting the muscles to the brain.
baby.102: ✦Your baby can move the arms and legs at the joints much faster and turn the head from side to side. Active enough to somersault, punch and kick, your baby practically does acrobatics in your belly. The umbilical cord, made of 3 blood vessels, gives the flexibility for these movements. Your baby can suck their fingers.
baby.103: ✦The baby still makes involuntary facial expressions.✦By making faces like surprise, sadness, anger and smiles, the baby is stretching and exercising the facial muscles.
baby.104: ✦There is still little fat under the skin.✦The baby's fine hair called lanugo has grown.✦Most of it falls out before birth and some after; it's thought to keep the baby warm until fat builds up in the skin.
baby.105: ✦Your baby's skin is still very thin.✦If you could look inside, you'd see the ribs and blood vessels under the skin.✦Babies are quite active now and use their waking time to move and stretch their muscles.✦Your baby may even have started sucking their thumb.
baby.106: ✦This week your baby is excitedly moving their arms and legs.✦Sometime between this week and week twenty, you may feel movement for the first time.✦Still, your baby is very small – about 11.5 to 12 cm and around 85 grams – and the cushion of amniotic fluid makes movements hard to feel at this point.
baby.107: ✦As you've probably noticed, sleeping on your stomach is almost impossible by now.✦Lying on your back is thought to put pressure on the main vein returning blood to your heart, so lying on your left side is best.✦Sleeping in this position improves circulation and minimises the chance of swelling (oedema) and varicose veins.
baby.108: ✦Your baby keeps making facial expressions like surprise, sadness, frowning and smiling.✦Don't worry – these aren't real emotional reactions; they're involuntary.✦Think of them as practice and exercises for the facial muscles.
baby.109: ✦Your baby can make grasping movements with their hands.✦They can even clasp their hands together or hold the umbilical cord.✦The hair is starting to get thicker.
baby.110: ✦At 16 weeks your baby keeps swallowing amniotic fluid and passing it through the digestive system as urine.✦In baby girls, hundreds of thousands of eggs form in the ovaries this week.✦The baby can kick with those tiny feet.
baby.111: ✦The eyes become more sensitive to light.✦The ears have started to hear.✦The placenta, which completed its development around weeks 12–13, lets the baby breathe, feed and get rid of waste.✦It also protects the baby from infections.✦It works very fast and uses a lot of energy, like an organ.✦That's why it receives a large blood supply.✦As the fetus grows and needs more, the placenta will thicken.✦The placenta is now about 1 cm thick and about 7–8 cm across.
baby.112: ✦On ultrasound your doctor can see your baby's body structures; organs such as the heart, diaphragm and kidneys can be observed.✦Your doctor can also check blood flow in the placenta and umbilical cord.
baby.113: ✦The hair, eyebrows and eyelashes are growing.✦The baby can open and close their mouth.✦They can move their closed eyes.✦Your baby is gaining weight along with you, but doesn't have enough fat yet because the fat-storing tissue has only just started to form.
baby.114: ✦All the major systems inside your baby are almost complete. The heart can beat 140–150 times a minute.✦The respiratory system is developing too; the chest is making breathing movements.
baby.115: ✦Feeling your baby grow inside you must be one of the most beautiful feelings in the world.✦At the same time you're probably curious about what's happening in there and how your baby is developing.
baby.116: ✦The baby's arms, legs, head and body are now in proportion.✦The skin keeps changing; fat is starting to build up and sweat glands are developing.✦This fat protects the baby.✦It also produces body heat, keeping the baby warm.✦As fat builds up, your baby will become chubbier before birth.
baby.117: ✦This week the baby starts storing calcium.✦So it's good to keep eating calcium-rich foods.✦The baby's heartbeat has started to be regulated by the brain.
baby.118: ✦The placenta keeps growing with your baby, managing the exchange between mother and baby and filtering out carbon dioxide.✦The baby can hear sounds and sense bright light through your belly.
baby.119: ✦Everything is fine in the body systems and they're working well.✦The digestive system is always working because the baby swallows amniotic fluid and urinates.✦Meanwhile, the baby keeps practising breathing.
baby.120: ✦Your baby can now hear much better, so communicating with them becomes even more enjoyable.✦Talk and sing to your baby whenever you can – they can hear both you and your partner.✦If you gently push on your belly while talking, they'll feel you.✦You can also play classical music.✦The more you communicate, the better your baby will recognise your voice in the coming weeks.✦They can hear your heartbeat and the sounds of your organs.✦Their own heart rate may change in response to outside sounds.✦If you go to a lively concert, your baby may make fast, jumping movements.
baby.121: ✦Your baby's sex organs have developed.✦In baby girls millions of eggs have formed.✦By birth this number drops to 1–2 million.✦The uterus and vaginal canal have started to form.✦In baby boys, development of the prostate is completed this week.✦The testicles haven't yet descended from the abdomen into the scrotum.✦In both boys and girls, the mammary glands and nipples have developed.
baby.122: ✦Stool called meconium starts to form in the intestines.✦As breathing practice speeds up, the sucking and swallowing reflexes develop too.✦Your baby can swallow amniotic fluid.✦Because the baby passes it as urine, the amniotic fluid is constantly renewed.✦With enough amniotic fluid, the lungs develop healthily.✦Although babies get oxygen and nutrients from the placenta until birth, the lungs must expand and contract in amniotic fluid to prepare for breathing after birth.
baby.123: ✦The ability to grasp keeps developing.✦With those tiny, thin fingers your baby can hold their face or the umbilical cord.✦Your baby may yawn when sleepy.✦You may feel hiccups as little rhythmic jumps.✦Even with closed eyes, the baby can move them left and right.✦Babies can sleep for 20 minutes to 2 hours at a time in the womb.
baby.124: ✦You can see your baby's arm and leg movements.✦The baby may be seen opening and closing the mouth.✦On ultrasound they may stick out their tongue.
baby.125: ✦Your baby is about 14 cm long and keeps growing quickly.✦They now have a daily routine and sleep habits.✦If it's a boy, the genitals can easily be seen on ultrasound.✦If you're having a girl, the uterus and fallopian tubes have formed and settled into place.
baby.126: ✦Unique fingerprints are beginning to form and the grip is getting stronger.✦The ears are working and can react to loud noises from outside.✦These reactions may come as kicks.✦But if this is your first pregnancy, you may not notice these soft sensations yet.
baby.127: ✦Air sacs are developing in the tiny lungs.✦Your baby may already have hiccups, but you can't feel them yet.
baby.128: ✦Your baby is 16–18 cm long, about the size of a small melon.✦It weighs about 240–250 grams.
baby.129: ✦Something important is about to happen: a layer called vernix will start to form on the baby's skin.✦This layer is thickest in the last 3 months.✦Some of it is still on the body when the baby is born.✦It protects the baby's skin from the acidity of the amniotic fluid.✦It also helps the baby slide through the birth canal during delivery.
baby.130: ✦The baby's whole body, including the eyelids and upper lip, is covered with a fine layer of hair (lanugo).
baby.131: ✦As muscle development continues, the baby gets stronger.✦Since starting to move the arms weeks ago, the baby can now throw quicker punches and kicks.✦The fat under the baby's skin keeps thickening.✦This fat helps maintain body temperature.✦It also keeps the baby warm after birth.
baby.132: ✦The baby's nervous system keeps building connections between the brain and every part of the body.✦This supports rapid development of the senses.✦At 19 weeks your baby can hear sounds very well.✦They can hear the sounds inside you, especially your heartbeat and the sounds of your stomach and intestines.✦They may react to loud outside noises with a jumpy movement.✦The sense of taste also starts to develop this week.✦Your baby can taste the amniotic fluid.
baby.133: ✦Your baby's sex organs have developed.✦In baby girls about 6 million eggs have formed this week.✦By birth this number drops to 1–2 million.✦The uterus and vaginal canal of a baby girl develop this week.✦In baby boys, the prostate finished developing last week.✦The testicles haven't yet descended from the abdomen into the scrotum.
baby.134: ✦On ultrasound your uterus may appear a little low.✦Don't worry – the uterus grows both up and down during pregnancy.✦The placenta, however, is not expected to be low this week.
baby.135: ✦Your baby continues to mature.✦The nails and eyebrows have started to appear.✦The hair that began growing earlier keeps growing.✦The baby keeps swallowing and practising breathing.✦The baby can open and close their mouth regularly.✦They can stick out their tongue.
baby.136: ✦Your baby is 17–19 cm long, about the size of a banana.✦It weighs about 300 grams.
baby.137: ✦In girls the uterus keeps developing; in boys the testicles begin moving down from the abdomen.✦It will take a few months for the testicles to fully descend into the scrotum.
baby.138: ✦Your baby spends part of the time sleeping.✦Sleep can last from 20 minutes to 2 hours.✦Although they can move their eyes left and right, the eyelids are still closed.✦As thin layers of fat form under the skin, the skin is getting thicker.✦So your baby keeps gaining weight.
baby.139: ✦The baby's skin is covered with a layer of fine hair called lanugo.✦This hair starts to disappear after 36 weeks.✦Very little remains after birth.✦What's left falls out within a few months.
baby.140: ✦The vernix caseosa layer on the skin, which started forming last week and will decrease over time, keeps increasing this week.✦This fatty substance contains 40–50 different proteins.✦Vernix protects the baby against various infections in the womb and in the days after birth.✦It also protects the baby's skin from the acidity of the amniotic fluid.✦This thick, creamy coating also makes it easier for the baby to pass through the birth canal.
baby.141: ✦This week your baby will taste whatever you eat and start getting used to – and liking – those flavours.✦That's because the amniotic fluid tastes different every day depending on what you eat (hot pepper one day, banana the next), and your baby now swallows this fluid daily (to stay hydrated, get nourishment and practise swallowing and digesting).
baby.142: ✦Your baby is now about 26 cm long and weighs 310 g.✦As hearing develops, they can hear you talking, singing and laughing.✦Your baby's organs can now absorb small amounts of sugar from the fluid they swallow.✦This sugar reaches the intestines and leaves the body as waste.✦The kidneys can now process waste more efficiently.
baby.143: ✦The baby's digestive system will start absorbing energy-giving nutrients from the amniotic fluid they swallow.✦But most of the baby's nutritional needs are still met by the placenta.
baby.144: ✦The skin is now fully covered with vernix caseosa.✦Most of this thick, paste-like protective coating, important for the immune system, disappears before birth.
baby.145: ✦Organ development is largely complete.✦Bone marrow formation is speeding up.✦Your baby's brain keeps growing rapidly, and this growth will continue for at least a few years after birth.
baby.146: ✦The baby's senses keep developing.✦With a developing sense of taste, your baby notices your eating habits.✦If you eat something sweet like chocolate, they may move more.✦They're increasingly aware of light and noise from outside.
baby.147: ✦Thanks to the amniotic fluid, your baby's development continues.✦This fluid protects the baby from bumps.✦By swallowing amniotic fluid, the baby also fills and empties the lungs, practising breathing.✦This prepares them for breathing after birth.✦The fluid also keeps the baby's digestive system working.
baby.148: ✦For a few weeks, stool called meconium has been forming in the intestines.✦The baby will keep storing it in the intestines until birth.✦Normally the baby doesn't pass this stool before birth.
baby.149: ✦This week your baby is about 28–29 cm long, the size of a large zucchini.✦It weighs about 430–450 grams.
baby.150: ✦The lungs keep developing and will start producing a substance (surfactant) that allows breathing after birth.
baby.151: ✦Your baby's thin, pink skin is now covered with vernix.✦The amount of fat under the skin keeps increasing.✦Two distinct skin layers are forming: the outer layer (epidermis) and the deeper layer (dermis).✦The epidermis that will form the prints on the fingers, toes, palms and soles keeps developing.✦There are tiny blood vessels in the lower skin layer.✦On top is the fine hair called lanugo.✦The paste-like vernix covering the skin decreases until birth.✦Babies born early still have a thick layer; babies born late may have less.
baby.152: ✦As brain cells develop and the brain sends signals to nerve endings throughout the body, the senses keep developing.✦This week the sense of touch develops further.✦Reflex movements are giving way to more conscious actions.✦Now your baby touches their face and holds the cord more deliberately!✦These new experiences must make them feel happy.
baby.153: ✦Although for now they only taste amniotic fluid, the sense of taste has fully developed – enough to tell bitter, sweet and sour.✦So your baby may react to your eating habits and the taste of what you eat.✦For example, if you eat something sweet, they may move more.✦Everything you eat passes through the placenta.✦The more vegetables, salads and fruits you eat during pregnancy, the more likely your child is to enjoy them later.
baby.154: ✦The reactions aren't only to taste.✦Your baby can now jump at loud, lively music.✦It's best to play calming music such as classical.✦Slow music like this helps your baby stay calmer.✦The baby can hear their parents' voices.✦If you talk to them a lot, they're very likely to recognise your voice after birth.
baby.155: ✦While red blood cells are being made, a substance called bilirubin is also produced.✦It's filtered by the liver and removed in the urine.✦If it hasn't all been cleared by the day of birth, it can take a few days to leave the body.✦A build-up of bilirubin causes jaundice after birth.✦This usually clears with sunlight and plenty of breastfeeding.
baby.156: ✦Your baby is about 29–30 cm long, the size of a large eggplant.✦It weighs about 500 grams.
baby.157: ✦Your baby's brain cells and senses keep developing.✦With more developed senses, their movements become more deliberate.✦As awareness grows, they're ready for new discoveries in taste, touch and hearing.
baby.158: ✦Communicating with your baby is good for them.✦Recognising your and your partner's voices will help them feel calm when they hear you after birth.
baby.159: ✦Babies can also hear their mother's heartbeat.✦That's why babies placed on their mother's chest after birth often calm down right away.✦Skin-to-skin contact, which keeps mother and baby together after birth, matters for this reason.✦In recent years, mother- and baby-friendly birth practices aim to keep mother and baby together after birth if there's no medical reason not to.✦During this time, skin-to-skin contact and breastfeeding are encouraged.✦Often the second person to hold the baby is the father, introducing the baby to the family's microbes.✦It's said that babies who stay with their mother for the first 45 minutes feel more secure later in life.✦This closeness also strengthens the bond between mother and baby.✦If this matters to you, talk to your doctor about your post-birth preferences and ask for skin-to-skin contact.
baby.160: ✦As your baby keeps swallowing amniotic fluid to practise breathing and keep the digestive system working, the lungs continue to mature.✦The lungs are producing surfactant, which will make breathing possible after birth.✦From next week your baby will reach the stage where they could survive outside the womb with medical help.
baby.161: ✦The fat layer under your baby's skin keeps increasing, but blood vessels are still visible.✦The thick, paste-like fatty layer on the skin called vernix caseosa keeps forming.✦It protects both the baby's warmth and immune system.✦This slippery coating also makes passing through the birth canal easier.
baby.162: ✦The nails and hair keep growing.✦Your baby sleeps in your belly and keeps waking up and moving.✦Your baby's eyes are flickering, but it'll be another 3–4 weeks before the eyelids open and close.
baby.163: ✦Your baby is now about 30 cm long and weighs 600 g.✦They look just like a small baby; proportions are right and the face has formed in full detail.✦The tiny air sacs and blood vessels in the lungs keep developing.✦If your baby were born this week, the lungs would be ready to work with artificial support.
baby.164: ✦Since the development that lets the lungs breathe in the outside world is largely complete, from this week your baby could survive with medical help if born early.✦That's why in the USA a 24-week baby is considered viable.✦In the UK the legal threshold of viability is also set at 24 weeks.
baby.165: ✦Your baby's senses are largely developed.✦As brain cells develop, the baby can respond more consciously and perception has improved.
baby.166: ✦Your baby can hear sounds very well now.✦Play calming music and talk to your baby whenever you can.✦Saying loving, positive words can help them feel good.✦You can even plan the birth together by talking to them.✦If you tell them you'll have a healthy, positive birth together, they'll feel it.✦You may be surprised how such words reflect positively on the birth.
baby.167: ✦The sense of touch is working nicely too.✦For example, if you gently press your belly, your baby may feel it and respond.
baby.168: ✦Your baby's movements keep getting faster.✦There's still plenty of room, so they're busy testing their developing muscles.✦You may feel some of these movements.✦The development of the senses shows in the movements.✦For example, you may notice jumps when they hear loud music, or more movement when you eat something sweet like chocolate.
baby.169: ✦You can see your baby moving on ultrasound.✦The grasping ability is developing well.✦You may see them easily bring their thin fingers to their face and even hold the umbilical cord.
baby.170: ✦Your baby is about 35–36 cm long, the size of a large zucchini.✦It weighs about 670 grams.
baby.171: ✦Your baby has come an incredible way from the size of a poppy seed.✦They're now a little baby whose development is largely complete.
baby.172: ✦Under US law the baby is now considered a person.✦Even if the lungs aren't fully developed yet, there's a chance of survival with medical help.
baby.173: ✦Although fat keeps building up under the skin, the body still looks thin.✦The vernix caseosa layer on the skin keeps helping to control body temperature.
baby.174: ✦Although your baby's skin keeps getting thicker, there are still capillaries near the surface, so the skin looks pink.✦It's also wrinkled.✦The formation of the skin layers (outer epidermis and deeper dermis) is complete.
baby.175: ✦Your baby's heart beats 140–150 times a minute.✦With all the senses working, your baby keeps exploring through them.✦They may react to loud sounds.✦They may relax to calm music.✦The sense of taste develops further.✦When you eat something sweet, they move more.
baby.176: ✦The skull bones are still soft, so the brain can keep growing easily.✦A soft skull is also what helps the baby pass through the birth canal during birth.✦The skull stays soft after birth too.✦It hardens over time.
baby.177: ✦Your baby is about 36–37 cm long, the size of a large squash.✦It weighs about 780 grams.
baby.178: ✦Your baby may sleep for 20 minutes to 2 hours at a time.✦Your baby will have their own sleep–wake pattern.✦If it doesn't match your routine, you may find yourself woken at midnight by kicks.
baby.179: ✦Your baby keeps swallowing amniotic fluid to practise breathing.✦They filter this fluid through the digestive system and pass it as urine.✦This helps increase the amount of amniotic fluid.✦Having enough amniotic fluid is vital for the baby.✦There's now about 500 ml of amniotic fluid.✦It's renewed every 3 hours.
baby.180: ✦The baby's heart rate has slowed compared with the early weeks.✦It beats 140–150 times a minute.✦The outer and deeper skin layers have formed.✦This week the skin starts producing pigment to gain its colour.
baby.181: ✦At the start of this week more hair has grown.✦The hair colour hasn't formed yet.✦Some babies are born bald, others with a full head of hair, some of which falls out.✦Some babies are born with dark hair that lightens within a few months.✦The opposite can happen too: a baby may be born with light hair that darkens within a few months.
baby.182: ✦The nails, eyebrows and eyelashes are being completed.✦Hand and footprints are becoming clearer.✦The whole body is covered with fine hair called lanugo.✦Lanugo supports skin development and keeps the body warm.✦Most of it falls out before birth.✦The rest will fall out within a few months after birth.
baby.183: ✦The vernix caseosa layer (a thick, fatty coating) that has been on the skin for 5–6 weeks will keep controlling body temperature until there's more fat under the skin.✦Although it decreases before birth, some is still on the baby at delivery.✦The remaining vernix also helps the baby pass through the birth canal.
baby.184: ✦Your baby has more taste buds in the mouth now than at birth.✦This means they not only notice what you eat through the amniotic fluid but may react to it.✦For example, some babies respond to spicy food with hiccups.✦Or they may kick when they taste spices.
baby.185: ✦From week 27 the fat under the skin will increase faster.✦Fat is also building up around the organs.✦In the last 3 months of pregnancy your baby will come a long way toward being chubby.✦As fat builds up, the fine hair on the skin (lanugo) will fall out, leaving the job of keeping warm to the fat.
baby.186: ✦As connections between the brain and nerve endings increase, the senses are completing their development.✦Since your baby started opening and closing their eyelids last week, the eyes are more sensitive to light.✦If a bright light shines on your belly, they may squint.
baby.187: ✦The brain – and so the head – keeps growing.✦As signals from the brain to nerve cells increase, the baby moves more consciously.✦Research suggests a primitive memory forms in these weeks.✦Studies also suggest that from this week babies store the language (even a different one) or songs they hear often in their memory.
baby.188: ✦Are you ready for tiny punches and kicks? We can almost hear you say, 'Goodness, what's going on with this baby?'✦Your baby is going through the most active period of the journey in the womb.✦Don't worry that your child will be hyperactive!✦It's far too early to think that.✦Babies move so much because they enjoy exploring their developing senses and there's still plenty of room.✦There's also plenty of amniotic fluid for their acrobatics.
baby.189: ✦Your baby has started making regular breathing movements by swallowing amniotic fluid.✦You may feel these as hiccups and see them on ultrasound.✦Even though they make breathing movements, the placenta still provides all the oxygen the baby needs.
baby.190: ✦As pregnancy progresses, the baby's movement and sleep settle into a pattern.✦There are periods of more or less activity lasting 1–3 hours.✦But if your baby is unusually still and not as active as usual, it's a good idea to talk to your doctor.
baby.191: ✦At this point babies are about 37.6 cm long and weigh about 1,005 g.✦This is considered an important week for babies.✦Research shows babies born in these weeks have a very good chance of survival.
baby.192: ✦Although a baby is expected to weigh 1,100 to 1,300 grams now, every baby develops differently.✦These numbers are averages; a heavier or lighter baby doesn't mean there's a problem.✦What matters is that your doctor sees no issue in the growth curve.
baby.193: ✦The surface of the baby's developing brain used to be smooth.✦Now the characteristic grooves and folds form on its surface.✦The amount of brain tissue also increases.
baby.194: ✦This week fat keeps building up under the skin.✦So the baby no longer looks as thin and is starting to fill out.✦The eyebrows and eyelashes form and the baby can now blink those tiny eyes.✦So this week's skill is blinking! Coughing, sucking, hiccupping and breathing movements are on the list too.
baby.195: ✦It's very common to ask about the baby's position at this stage.✦It's impossible to tell the position just by touching the belly.✦The baby changes position throughout pregnancy.✦In the last trimester the head is most likely to be down, but your doctor will give the most accurate information during an ultrasound.
baby.196: ✦This week fat under the baby's skin is building up faster.✦Fat will keep building up until birth and your baby will look adorable.✦Fat is also forming around the organs.
baby.197: ✦The baby's body systems are working wonderfully.✦The lungs are close to finishing the development needed to breathe in the outside world.✦If born early after this week, babies have a chance of survival, though they need medical help.
baby.198: ✦Your baby is about 39–40 cm long, the size of a pumpkin.✦It weighs about 1,200 grams.
baby.199: ✦With the first 6 months behind you, you must be feeling relieved.✦It's natural to feel impatient as the birth gets closer.✦Even if your baby is born early during these last 3 months, the chance of survival is high.✦Try to stay relaxed – about 90% of babies are born at or near term.
baby.200: ✦Most of the small airways (bronchioles) in the lungs are in place and the number of tiny air sacs (alveoli) has increased.✦Surfactant, which lowers surface tension inside the air sacs, keeps forming.✦Its production will be complete around week 35.✦As the lungs develop, the baby keeps breathing rhythmically to prepare for life after birth.
baby.201: ✦Your baby keeps sucking their finger, strengthening the sucking muscles.✦The facial muscles' ability to breastfeed will be complete around weeks 35–36.
baby.202: ✦This week the skin is pink and wrinkled.✦Fat under the skin is increasing.✦The part of the brain related to intelligence and temperament keeps developing.✦Reactions to different sounds, foods and light are more deliberate.
baby.203: ✦Red blood cells are developing in the bones.✦Even as the bones harden this week, they stay flexible.✦This flexibility continues after birth.✦The bones fully harden during childhood.✦The skull bones are soft too.✦After all, the bones need to be flexible for the baby to pass through the birth canal.✦The soft spots on the baby's skull, called fontanelles, close and harden within about 1–1.5 years after birth.
baby.204: ✦You've probably noticed the movement in your belly continues.✦There's even a rhythm and pattern to it.✦For example, the baby may be more active after you eat or when you rest.✦But if you notice the movements break from this pattern, don't hesitate to call your doctor.
baby.205: ✦This week your baby is about 40–41 cm long, the size of a cabbage.✦It weighs about 1,400 grams.
baby.206: ✦Your baby will gain about half a kilo every week.✦As fat under the skin increases, the fine lanugo hair that helped regulate temperature keeps falling out.✦Temperature control will now mostly be the job of the fat tissue.
baby.207: ✦This week your baby's senses are very developed.✦They can tell your voice from your partner's.✦They can react to different tastes and bright light through your belly.✦If you gently press toward your baby on your belly, they may first pull back and then push back in response.✦Having your partner do this helps their bond with the baby begin even before birth.
baby.208: ✦The baby needs plenty of calcium, protein and iron for bones, muscles and blood cells.✦If you don't get enough of these nutrients, the baby will take them from your reserves.
baby.209: ✦Your baby's brain is as developed as a newborn's.✦Still, brain cells keep developing.✦For brain development, being born at or near term is an advantage.
baby.210: ✦Your baby is enjoying the journey in your belly, sleeping and waking in turns.✦Just when you think they haven't moved for hours, a small but firm kick says, 'I'm awake now.'
baby.211: ✦As the baby's muscles get much stronger, so do the movements.✦Though they're a bit less frequent than in past weeks, strong punches, kicks and stretches can hurt.✦Some nights they may even be strong enough to wake you up.
baby.212: ✦Your baby is about 41–42 cm long, the length of a leek.✦It weighs about 1,400 grams.
baby.213: ✦Your baby's organs and body systems are almost fully formed.✦From now on, the biggest changes will be in length and weight.✦Weekly weight gain is about 500 grams on average.
baby.214: ✦This week the fine lanugo hair on your baby's skin keeps disappearing quickly.✦The vernix caseosa layer, which keeps the body warm and supports the immune system, has become much thicker.
baby.215: ✦The fingernails have fully grown; the toenails still have a way to go.✦The baby can now close and open the eyelids much better.✦The eyes' ability to see and focus is complete.✦The brain and nervous system are fully developed.✦So the baby moves more and more deliberately each day.
baby.216: ✦This week surfactant production in the baby's lungs continues, supported by the adrenal glands.✦Each week the lungs develop further toward breathing easily in the outside world.✦Since they'll keep maturing for about 5 more weeks, babies born after 36 weeks can breathe almost without help.
baby.217: ✦This week your baby's movements have slowed because there's less room.✦But that doesn't mean they'll stop moving.✦If your baby doesn't move for a while, tell your doctor.
baby.218: ✦Your baby is expected to be head-down (vertex position).✦But if your baby hasn't turned yet, don't worry right away.✦At this stage 25–30% of babies are still breech.✦Your baby may still turn head-down until week 38.✦About 4% of babies are born breech.
baby.219: ✦This week your baby is about 42–43 cm long, the size of a head of lettuce.✦It weighs about 1,700 grams.
baby.220: ✦All organs except the lungs are fully developed and working.✦So almost all babies born at this week or later survive.✦But they will need help breathing until about week 36.
baby.221: ✦Your baby is getting longer and the skin keeps filling out with fat.✦The toenails have mostly grown.✦The baby now spends two-thirds of the time sleeping.✦Research suggests the ability to dream starts developing from these weeks.
baby.222: ✦The heart rate is starting to slow a little.✦Your heartbeat can affect the baby's heart too.✦So it's good to keep your days as calm as possible.
baby.223: ✦All of your baby's organs except the lungs and digestive system are ready.✦When awake, they can do many things a newborn does.✦They can grab their feet and suck their fingers.✦The eyelashes, eyebrows and hair are now visible.✦They can make many facial expressions.
baby.224: ✦Although space is getting tight, your baby is still active.✦With much stronger muscles now, you may feel movements as strong jabs.✦Tiny blows or stretches can sometimes hurt.✦You can now tell better whether a jab comes from a hand or a foot.✦Some babies are calm in the womb, others very active until birth.✦This activity level usually continues after birth.✦The same goes for the sleep–wake cycle.✦If your baby sleeps for long stretches in your belly, their sleep routine will probably be similar after birth.
baby.225: ✦From this week, your doctor won't order frequent ultrasounds unless needed.✦In some countries ultrasounds are done much more often than elsewhere.✦Since possible effects on the baby haven't been fully ruled out, fewer ultrasounds are generally better; if all is well, you can ask your doctor for fewer scans.
baby.226: ✦This week the baby gains about 225 grams on average compared with last week.✦By the big day your baby's weight may almost double.
baby.227: ✦There's enough amniotic fluid at this stage.✦A low level of fluid isn't healthy.✦Your baby keeps breathing regularly and making breathing movements by swallowing amniotic fluid.✦But they still get most of their oxygen from the placenta.
baby.228: ✦Brain cells are still developing.✦Brain cell development is very important for skills after birth.✦By this week, most of the fine lanugo hair that covered the baby's body has fallen out.✦The vernix caseosa layer on the skin has become quite thick and now keeps your baby warm enough.
baby.229: ✦The baby's hair has fully grown.✦Your baby might also have no hair.✦Babies born without hair usually have relatively little until age 1, and it starts to grow after that.
baby.230: ✦Your baby's space is getting tighter.✦So tiny but strong jabs and stretches may hurt more and more.✦You can have fun feeling their hiccups.
baby.231: ✦This week babies keep moving their arms, legs, body and head.✦They keep sucking their thumb or other fingers to develop the sucking muscles.✦This way the facial muscles will be ready to breastfeed after birth.
baby.232: ✦The amniotic fluid level has peaked.✦With no room for more fluid, you may be more bothered by your baby's nudges and kicks.✦That's because there's less fluid to cushion them and your baby is bigger.
baby.233: ✦This week your baby is about 45–46 cm long, the size of a honeydew melon.✦It weighs about 2,100–2,300 grams.
baby.234: ✦Perhaps the most striking thing this week is that your baby fully feels whatever you're doing.✦What you eat and drink, sounds from outside, your mood – everything affects them, even how much they move.
baby.235: ✦The vernix caseosa layer on your baby's skin keeps regulating body temperature and keeping the skin moist.✦This white, paste-like coating will decrease before birth.✦It will also make it easier for the baby to pass through the birth canal.
baby.236: ✦The lungs keep maturing and will be fully developed in 2–3 weeks. Babies born at 34 weeks can survive, but may need to stay in an incubator for 2–3 weeks to get breathing support.
baby.237: ✦At 34 weeks the baby's brain cells keep developing. This is important for the baby's skills in the outside world! Like all the senses, memory and the ability to remember are developed.
baby.238: ✦You keep producing antibodies to prepare your baby for the outside world.✦At this stage most babies have settled into the birth position.✦If you could see inside, you'd notice your baby's nails are long enough to reach past the fingertips.✦If it's a boy, the testicles can now be seen.
baby.239: ✦Your baby's central nervous system and lungs keep developing and are very close to their final form.✦If you're worried about an early birth, try not to be afraid: babies born at this stage have almost completed their development and usually do very well.
baby.240: ✦This week your baby is about 46–47 cm long, the size of a large melon.✦It weighs about 2,400 grams.
baby.241: ✦Your baby is now aware enough to be preparing for birth.✦To leave the womb easily, they've probably turned head-down (cephalic position). If your baby hasn't turned yet this week, wait a few more weeks.✦About 96% of babies turn head-down before birth.✦In the final weeks, a head-down baby should ideally face your back (anterior position).✦This position is also an advantage for caesarean births.
baby.242: ✦The brain and nervous system are fully developed.✦The number of brain cells keeps increasing.
baby.243: ✦The fine hair (lanugo) on the baby's skin keeps falling out.✦The thick, white, creamy vernix caseosa that has been forming on the skin for weeks controls body temperature and protects the skin from the acidity of the amniotic fluid.✦It also helps the baby pass through the birth canal.✦In natural birth practices, the vernix is left on the skin for a while after birth – the baby isn't bathed right away.✦This way the coating keeps moisturising and nourishing the skin as the baby adapts to the outside world.✦Even if the baby is bathed within 12–24 hours, it's done so that some vernix stays on the body.
baby.244: ✦Although the skull bones keep hardening, they're still soft.✦The skull bones haven't joined yet.✦There are soft tissues between them called fontanelles.✦These soft spots on the baby's head only close and harden fully by the time the baby is 1–1.5 years old.
baby.245: ✦The baby's first black stool, called meconium, keeps collecting in the large intestine.✦Babies normally don't pass it before birth.✦Passing it in the womb can be a health risk.✦If this is noticed, the doctor's decisions should be followed carefully.
baby.246: ✦Your baby has little room but still moves strongly between naps.✦You may feel hiccups too.✦If the head is down, you'll sometimes feel your baby's bottom under your ribs.✦Some mothers say they can clearly feel the pressure of their baby's feet and toes in these weeks.
baby.247: ✦This week your baby is about 47–48 cm long, the size of a large head of lettuce.✦It weighs about 2,600–2,700 grams.
baby.248: ✦This week you may worry, 'My baby used to kick hard, now they seem to move less.'✦But your baby's space is tight now, and they're counting the days to come out.✦There used to be room for every kind of movement in the womb.✦Now things are cramped, though there's still room to turn and wriggle.
baby.249: ✦Once the head settles deep in the pelvis, the baby will move even less.✦So it's completely normal to feel fewer movements at 36 weeks.✦Don't expect wild somersaults and kicks like before. But if you notice anything unusual in the movements, be sure to talk to your doctor.
baby.250: ✦You're not the only one who can't wait for your baby to arrive.✦Your little one is also aware that the journey in your belly is nearing its end.✦Your baby is preparing for birth in every way.✦Although there are about 4–6 weeks to go, they should already be in the birth position.✦Most likely the head is down and settled into the pelvis, waiting.
baby.251: ✦The baby keeps getting longer.✦Fat keeps building up under the skin and around the organs and some muscles.✦Although surfactant production is still going on, the lungs are largely developed.✦If born this week, your baby could probably breathe without help.✦The sucking muscles will be fully developed by the end of this week, ready to breastfeed.✦The digestive system is ready too.
baby.252: ✦The heart beats 110–150 times a minute.✦The placenta is now 20–25 cm across and 2–3 cm thick.✦This precious organ – practically everything to the baby during pregnancy – will weigh 700–750 grams at birth.
baby.253: ✦This week black stool called meconium keeps being produced in the baby's large intestine.✦If the baby is under stress, they may pass it.✦If your waters break this week and the fluid is dark, the baby may have passed this stool in the womb.✦In that case the doctor may decide to start labour.
baby.254: ✦This week your baby is about 48–49 cm long, the length of a long chard stalk.✦It weighs about 2,800–2,900 grams.
baby.255: ✦Even though there are about 3 weeks left until your due week, your baby should already be in the birth position.✦Most likely the head is down and settled into the pelvis, waiting.
baby.256: ✦The baby keeps getting longer.✦Fat keeps building up under the skin and around the organs and some muscles.✦This fat will help your baby control body temperature, grow and thrive after birth.
baby.257: ✦At this stage the lungs are largely developed.✦If born this week, your baby could probably breathe without help.✦Finger movements and grasping have developed further.✦The baby can grasp not only their hands but also their face or toes.✦By the end of this week the sucking muscles will be fully developed, ready to breastfeed.✦The digestive system is ready for breast milk.✦The heart beats 110–150 times a minute.
baby.258: ✦This week black stool called meconium keeps being produced in the baby's large intestine.✦If babies are under stress, they may pass it in the womb.✦If your waters break this week and the fluid is dark, the baby may have passed this stool in the womb.✦In that case the doctor may decide to start labour.
baby.259: ✦The placenta has reached its maximum size and thickness (about 25 cm across and 2–3 cm thick).✦It will weigh 700–750 grams at birth.✦At 37 weeks, the testicles in baby boys have almost fully descended into the scrotum.
baby.260: ✦Your baby knows your and your partner's voices very well.✦Their vision improves every week.✦This week antibodies start passing from mother to baby through the umbilical cord.✦These antibodies prepare the baby for the illnesses and germs they'll meet outside the womb.
baby.261: ✦This week your baby is about 49–50 cm long, the size of a medium watermelon.✦It weighs about 3,000 grams.
baby.262: ✦If your baby is born this week, they'll be fully developed, so you can relax.✦It's normal for babies to be born between 38 and 42 weeks.✦But some doctors, in many countries, wait until 41 weeks at most.✦Since the risk at 42 weeks is very low for the baby, natural-birth doctors may wait until 42 weeks in pregnancies where everything is fine.✦Waiting beyond 42 weeks isn't recommended, because the placenta's function drops a lot after that and it can be risky for the baby.✦If all is well and you want to wait, discuss this preference with your doctor in advance.
baby.263: ✦The baby is fully mature, but brain cells keep increasing.✦So staying in the womb a little longer can still be an advantage.✦Connections are forming in the brain that will help them adapt better.✦Breathing skills and the digestive system keep getting better.
baby.264: ✦This week the baby's heart beats 110–150 times a minute.
baby.265: ✦Your baby's first stool, a dark green to black substance called meconium, will contain dead skin cells and lanugo.✦The lungs keep maturing and producing more surfactant (which will stop the air sacs sticking together when your baby starts breathing).✦At this stage your baby can hear your voice.✦So you and your partner should talk to them often.
baby.266: ✦Most of the body hair has fallen out, but some babies are born with patches of lanugo that fall out in the first days or weeks.✦Since the sucking and swallowing muscles developed, your baby has been taking in amniotic fluid, and waste collects in the intestines.
baby.267: ✦You're nearing the end of your pregnancy, and your baby keeps growing fast.✦This week is important in pregnancy.✦Your baby is now just about ready to manage on their own and adapt to the outside world.
baby.268: ✦This week your baby is about 50–51 cm long, the size of a large pumpkin.✦It weighs about 3,300 grams.
baby.269: ✦Your baby is mature enough to live comfortably in the outside world if born now.✦Still, brain cells keep increasing.✦Brain development in the womb is very valuable.✦In years when this wasn't known, babies born by planned caesarean were delivered at 38 weeks.✦Fortunately, unless there's a medical need, planned caesareans now require the baby to be at least 39 weeks.
baby.270: ✦By this week most of the fine lanugo hair on the baby's body has fallen out.✦At 39 weeks, the vernix caseosa on your baby's skin keeps controlling body temperature and keeping the skin moist.✦It will also make it easier for the baby to pass through the birth canal.✦In natural birth practices, the vernix is left on the skin for a while after birth – the baby isn't bathed right away.✦This way the coating keeps the skin moist and nourished as the baby adapts to the outside world.✦At the first bath, the baby is washed so that some vernix stays on the skin.
baby.271: ✦This week antibodies keep passing from mother to baby through the umbilical cord.✦Thanks to them, the baby will be ready for the illnesses and germs they'll meet outside the womb.
baby.272: ✦This week fat keeps building up under the skin and around the organs and some muscles.✦Thanks to this fat, your baby's body will be able to control its temperature after birth.✦They'll need this fat for healthy growth and to thrive.
baby.273: ✦Your baby moves less because space is tight.✦But you can still feel those tiny hands and feet pushing as they stretch.✦As the baby settles head-first into the pelvis to prepare for birth, you may feel pain and aches low down.✦In these weeks you'll feel hiccups as small rhythmic jumps.✦Since your baby moves when awake, it's good to keep track of the movements.✦If you don't feel movement for a while, be sure to talk to your doctor.
baby.274: ✦Your baby should be in the birth position.✦Most likely the head is down and settled into the pelvis, waiting.✦In the ideal birth position, the baby faces the mother's spine.✦But the face may be turned right, left or forward.✦In such cases the baby may still move into the ideal position before birth.✦If not, the doctor may suggest turning the baby by hand.
baby.275: ✦This week your baby is about 51–52 cm long, the size of a watermelon.✦It weighs about 3,500 grams.
baby.276: ✦By the end of this week, the 9 months and 10 days of pregnancy will be complete.✦You may give birth this week.✦But things may not go as expected, and your baby may decide to stay a little longer.✦There's no need to worry if pregnancy goes past 40 weeks.✦According to medical guidelines, as long as everything is fine, the baby can be awaited until 42 weeks.✦In that case your doctor will suggest monitoring the baby more often.✦Some doctors wait until 41 weeks.✦How long doctors wait differs between hospitals and countries.✦Waiting times also vary between individual doctors.✦Many doctors who don't wait until 42 weeks prefer not to take on the legal risk.✦Doctors who do wait until 42 weeks trust the nature of mother and baby, are experienced in normal birth, and know there's no medical problem in waiting as long as all is well.
baby.277: ✦When your baby is born, the nurse clears mucus and amniotic fluid from the baby's mouth and nose.✦Surfactant, produced since the last trimester, does its job right after birth by helping the lungs inflate.✦This lets the baby breathe easily on arrival.✦Because premature babies haven't finished producing surfactant, they're given artificial surfactant and breathing support in an incubator.
baby.278: ✦When your baby comes out, you may see them still curled up in the fetal position.✦That's simply out of habit and comfort.✦After 9 months in a tight womb, it can take time for them to realise there's room to stretch out.
baby.279: ✦If you're not showing signs of labour yet, don't be disappointed.✦About 50% of pregnancies last longer than 40 weeks.✦Many doctors normally allow pregnancy to continue until 42 weeks.✦If labour doesn't start on its own, your doctor will induce it at 41 or 42 weeks.
baby.280: ✦Your baby is in your arms at last! You've reached the end of a 9-month marathon.✦And the lovely days ahead aren't limited to this excitement – first teeth, first milestones and the first birthday will keep adding new joys every day.✦'Look, they're crawling!', 'Look, a tooth!', 'They said mama/dada!' – the excitement never ends! 🙂

mother.1: ✦In the first week, the baby hasn't actually implanted in your womb yet.✦Pregnancy lasts 40 weeks, but it is counted from the first day of your last period, not from implantation. During the first week, an egg cell starts to develop in your left or right ovary.
mother.2: ✦Before your baby starts growing, you set the stage.✦Last week's rise in estrogen and progestin in your blood prompted your womb to build a rich, blood-filled lining ready for a possible fertilized egg.✦At the same time, eggs are maturing in fluid-filled sacs in your ovaries called follicles.
mother.3: ✦At the start of this week (usually around day 14 of a 28-day cycle) you ovulated.✦One of your eggs left its follicle and travelled to the fallopian tube.✦Over the next 12–24 hours, one of the roughly 250 million sperm released by your partner will swim through the vagina, pass the cervix, enter the womb and try to reach and enter the egg in the fallopian tube.✦If it succeeds, the egg will be fertilized.✦About 400 sperm survive this journey, and only one manages to break through the egg's membrane.
mother.4: ✦Over the next 30 hours, the nuclei of the sperm and the egg will join to combine their genetic material.✦If the sperm carries a Y chromosome, your baby will be a boy; if it carries an X chromosome, you'll have a girl.
mother.5: ✦On its 3–4 day journey from the fallopian tube to the womb, the fertilized egg – the zygote – divides into 16 identical cells.✦Once it reaches the womb, the zygote is called a morula.✦One or two days later it settles into the lining of your womb and continues its amazing development and transformation.
mother.6: ✦At this stage your developing baby is just a tiny ball of cells, scientifically called a blastocyst.✦The blastocyst has an inner cell mass that will form the embryo and an outer cell mass that will form the placenta; there is also a fluid-filled cavity that will become the amniotic sac.✦The outer cell mass becomes the placenta, the organ that brings oxygen and nutrients to your baby and carries waste away.
mother.7: ✦Your last period started 12 to 16 days ago.✦So you're probably ovulating now or will ovulate soon.✦Although pregnancy really lasts about 38 weeks, the exact moment egg and sperm meet can't be known, so doctors calculate the due date as 40 weeks from the start of your last period.✦That's why you're already counted as 2 weeks pregnant when fertilization happens.✦Timing really matters if you want to conceive.✦To improve your chances, have intercourse between 72 hours before and 24 hours after ovulation.✦This lines up the sperm's 72-hour lifespan with the egg's 24-hour lifespan.✦Your partner should keep this window free too.✦To ease the pressure on both of you, it helps to know how long conception usually takes.✦Most couples only announce a pregnancy after several tries.✦If you're trying to conceive and still drink, smoke or take medicines, now is the time to stop.✦Your body should be in the best possible shape for the baby.✦Talk to your doctor about starting folic acid and vitamin supplements to lower the risk of birth defects.
mother.8: ✦In the second week of pregnancy (around day 14 of a 28-day cycle) the released egg is pushed into the fallopian tube.✦Within the next 12 to 24 hours, out of about 250 million sperm making the tough 10-hour journey through the vagina, cervix and uterus to the fallopian tube, around 400 survive and only one enters the egg's membrane.✦The surge in LH peaks within 24 to 36 hours; this process, commonly known as ovulation, ends with the mature egg being fertilized by the right sperm.
mother.9: ✦When the due date is calculated, counting starts before fertilization – from week 2 – even though sperm and egg haven't met yet.✦Women have about a 25% chance of getting pregnant in each menstrual cycle.
mother.10: ✦At 2 weeks, the earliest stage of pregnancy, the sudden rise in estrogen and progesterone can make your breasts extra sensitive.✦But since this is also a symptom of the menstrual cycle, breast changes can't be taken as a definite sign of pregnancy.
mother.11: ✦Most babies are born around this week of the cycle count, but it's usually hard to know exactly when egg and sperm met.✦That's why health providers use 40 weeks from the first day of your last period to estimate the due date.✦These estimates can vary by about 4 weeks depending on the length of your cycle.✦Since some women have shorter or longer cycles, the due date can be pinned down more precisely with an ultrasound.
mother.12: ✦Timing is very important for fertilization.✦Your chances of conceiving are highest in the window around ovulation, roughly two weeks before your next period would start.✦Beyond all this, most couples need more than a few tries before conceiving.✦So it's important to have a full health check-up before deciding to have a baby to make sure you're ready.✦If you take any medication, be sure to tell your doctor and decide whether to continue it during pregnancy.
mother.13: ✦Every baby develops a little differently, even in the womb.✦If you think you need vitamin supplements, talk to your doctor and, if needed, start them from this week.✦Folic acid in particular is very important for the baby's development and for protecting against harm in the womb.✦Also make sure to eat plenty of nutrient-rich fruits and vegetables.
mother.14: ✦Besides building a healthy prenatal diet and exercise routine, this week is the perfect time to quit smoking and alcohol.
mother.15: ✦You're at the start of the first trimester (the first 3 months of pregnancy).✦The first trimester, which lasts until week 13, will be the period of the most change in your life until the moment you hold your baby.✦Mothers-to-be usually realise they're pregnant around this time, after a missed period.
mother.16: ✦Even if you don't look pregnant yet, your body is going through many changes inside and out.✦In the first trimester, when growth is fastest, you'll experience the development of your baby's brain, heart and spine together.
