mother.17: ✦Early pregnancy signs at 3 weeks vary from person to person and may include back pain, tiredness and mild cramps.
mother.18: ✦Tender, swollen breasts: many women describe this as much stronger than before a period.✦Exhaustion and tiredness: rising progesterone and your baby's development can make you feel like you've run a marathon.✦Needing to pee often: this starts right after you conceive.✦Heightened sense of smell: smells feeling stronger is a common sign.✦It's caused by the sudden rise in estrogen.✦Food aversions: aversion to certain foods is a more common sign than increased appetite.✦Nausea, vomiting and morning sickness: these usually begin a few weeks later.✦But some mothers-to-be notice them earlier.✦Higher body temperature: if your temperature has been slightly raised for more than 18 days, you're most likely pregnant.✦Light bleeding: you may have light red, pink or brown spotting around the time of your period.✦If you also have severe pain, contact your doctor right away.
mother.19: ✦At this stage, rather than cravings, you may find yourself turning away from foods – things you usually enjoy may suddenly seem off-putting.✦Many smells can also make you gag in early pregnancy.✦This is due to rapidly rising estrogen levels.✦Morning sickness isn't common yet, but in some pregnancies it starts a little earlier.
mother.20: ✦Now is the time to start paying more attention to your health than usual.✦Drinking plenty of water and eating 5 portions of different fruits and vegetables a day is enough for now.✦If you haven't yet, talk to your doctor about starting folic acid supplements.
mother.21: ✦Once you know you're pregnant, pay attention to everything you eat and drink.✦Coffee, tea and alcohol top the list.✦High caffeine intake in pregnancy may raise the risk of miscarriage and low birth weight.✦One cup of coffee a day is generally fine as long as caffeine stays under 200 milligrams.✦Remember tea contains caffeine too, so count it toward your limit.
mother.22: ✦At 4 weeks, your body is changing very actively.✦The changes vary from woman to woman.✦Some experience typical early symptoms like mood swings, nausea and cramps; others have uncomfortable PMS-like symptoms.✦Some women go through this stage without feeling any of these.✦Whether you feel them or not, it may still be too early for a pregnancy test to give a reliable result.
mother.23: ✦This week the fertilized egg and your womb are connected, and your baby – as a blastocyst – starts attaching to the uterine wall.✦In about 30% of pregnancies, implantation bleeding happens as the cell cluster burrows into the uterine wall.✦Implantation bleeding is usually very light and light pink, light red or light brown.✦It happens before your expected period and is not a sign that something is wrong.✦You may feel slight pressure in your belly (nothing to worry about!) and mild breast tenderness and growth (get ready for more growth spurts).
mother.24: ✦The fertilized egg burrows into the womb, and as a result you may have some light bleeding.✦Any pregnancy symptoms at this stage will be very subtle.✦If you're very sensitive, you may notice tiredness, nausea, bloating, tender breasts and changes in hair and skin.
mother.25: ✦Right after a positive pregnancy test, it's a good idea to see a GP or a dentist.✦Dental check-ups during pregnancy are really important.✦Besides caring for your teeth during pregnancy, keep it up during the first 12 months after birth too.
mother.26: ✦This week you may find out whether you're pregnant.✦For a clear result, wait until the end of this week and take a pregnancy test.✦If it's positive, call your doctor and book your first prenatal appointment.✦Many doctors don't schedule the first visit before week eight.✦But if you have a health problem, had a difficult pregnancy before, or have worrying symptoms, call your doctor right away.
mother.27: ✦The next 6 weeks will be very critical for your baby's development.✦The placenta and umbilical cord, still developing, will start taking on their jobs.✦Everything you take in will reach your baby through the placenta and directly affect their health and development.✦So pay close attention to your diet.
mother.28: ✦Welcome to the nausea club! Almost 75% of pregnant women are members.✦So this is something millions of pregnant women go through – no need to worry.
mother.29: ✦This week early pregnancy signs continue while your baby develops rapidly.✦As more signs of pregnancy appear day by day, your sesame-seed-sized baby keeps causing big changes in your body.✦This week you may experience frequent urination, excess saliva, cravings and food aversions.
mother.30: ✦This week the baby is 1.5–2 mm long, about the size of a sesame seed.✦It weighs very little – about 1.5 grams at most.
mother.31: ✦Your baby's development continues excitingly this week.✦Many mothers-to-be wonder if a 5-week baby can be seen on ultrasound.✦The first ultrasound is usually done transvaginally for a better assessment.✦Since the baby is still a rapidly developing cluster of cells, it appears as a tiny white dot.
mother.32: ✦On ultrasound a 5-week baby looks like a tiny tadpole.✦By the end of the week it starts to curve into a C shape, so it's also compared to a shrimp.✦Your doctor will measure your baby's length on the ultrasound.✦From this week the heart starts beating, though you won't hear it on the ultrasound yet.✦The heart, the first organ to start working, beats about 90–100 times a minute this week.✦The spinal cord will start forming between the brain and the tail.
mother.33: ✦Many women have vaginal discharge throughout pregnancy.✦Leukorrhea is a thin, white, mild-smelling or odourless discharge.✦It's caused by hormones and the growing blood flow to the vaginal walls.✦Discharge may increase throughout pregnancy. Its high acidity is thought to help keep harmful bacteria away.
mother.34: ✦You may have light vaginal bleeding or spotting during the first 12 weeks.✦Depending on how heavy, long and frequent it is, bleeding can mean many things.✦It's very important to keep track of it and inform your doctor accurately.✦Note the consistency (watery, thick), colour (light pink, light red, dark red, etc.), duration and frequency, and talk to your doctor.
mother.35: ✦Although it's called morning sickness, nausea isn't limited to mornings.✦It can happen at any time of day.✦It's most common in the first trimester, the first 3 months of pregnancy.✦Signs usually appear between weeks 5 and 8.✦It's expected to ease by weeks 13–14.
mother.36: ✦You may have gained a few kilos by now.✦If you have nausea and can't eat well, you may even have lost weight.✦If this is your first pregnancy, your belly may not have changed much yet, or your waistbands may feel a little tight.✦You may be gaining weight in your legs or breasts.
mother.37: ✦You may feel emotionally up and down – your hormones are at work.✦On top of that, huge changes are coming in your life.✦It's completely natural to feel intense emotions.
mother.38: ✦Light bleeding can happen at this stage.✦It doesn't mean the pregnancy is in trouble.✦But bleeding can also be the first sign of a miscarriage or ectopic pregnancy.✦If you have bleeding, it's still advisable to tell your doctor.
mother.39: ✦About 1 in 31 births is twins.✦Without fertility treatment, the chance drops to about 1 in 89.✦The chance of triplets (or more) is about 1 in 565.✦Identical twins usually happen by chance, about 1 in 250.✦20–25% of women who have fertility treatment conceive twins (or more).✦Your chance of twins can also depend on other factors.✦If you've had twins before, your chance of having twins again doubles.✦If there are twins in your or your partner's family, your chance is higher.✦The older you are, the higher the chance of naturally conceiving twins (or more).✦The more pregnancies you've had, the higher your chance.✦Twins are more common in tall, slim women and less common in shorter women.
mother.40: ✦It's very important to avoid foods and drinks that could harm you or your baby during pregnancy.✦But there's a lot of misinformation about which foods are good or bad.✦You don't want to skip healthy foods or stress about your diet because of it.✦So learn now which foods and drinks to avoid.✦At 6 weeks, keeping a list of these on your fridge can help.
mother.41: ✦From the first weeks of pregnancy, the mother's metabolism speeds up a lot to meet the baby's needs.✦The amount of blood pumped from the heart to the organs and skin increases by about 40%.✦Your blood volume will increase by nearly 50%.
mother.42: ✦At 6 weeks, changes in the mother become noticeable.✦Breast tenderness, growth and darkening of the nipples are signs of 6 weeks of pregnancy.✦Fat starts building up around the waist.
mother.43: ✦All roads lead to the bathroom.✦Surging hormones and increased blood volume make your body produce more fluid, so you'll find yourself heading to the toilet more often than ever.✦But keeping your body well hydrated is important, so keep drinking extra water throughout pregnancy.
mother.44: ✦Healthy habits.✦During pregnancy, order your meat well done and stay away from cat litter.✦Toxoplasmosis, an infection spread by raw meat and cat faeces, can be harmful to your baby (though not to you).✦You may already have had it without knowing – in that case you're immune.
mother.45: ✦Keep drinking plenty of water, even if it means more trips to the toilet.✦Make sure the meat you eat is well cooked.✦If there's a flu outbreak, get vaccinated (ask your doctor).
mother.46: ✦You may feel very emotional this week.✦You may develop aversions to some foods.✦Or you may strongly crave others.

mother.60: ✦Your kidneys working harder and the uterus pressing on your bladder may make you need to pee often.
mother.61: ✦At 9 weeks, nausea may still be intense for some mothers-to-be.✦Here are the causes of pregnancy nausea.✦A rise in the pregnancy hormone beta-hCG.✦This hormone starts to decline later in the first trimester.✦That's why nausea passes for many women between weeks 13 and 15.✦Sudden drops in blood sugar.✦That's why nausea is often worse when you wake up on an empty stomach.✦Nausea can also appear before other meals as blood sugar drops.✦Rising progesterone relaxes the stomach muscles and slows food moving into the intestines.✦This can increase stomach acid and therefore nausea.✦In cases of excessive vomiting, you may need to be hospitalised and given IV fluids to replace lost water, salt and sugar.
mother.62: ✦In the ninth week, some mothers-to-be may develop skin problems.✦Drinking plenty of water, eating healthily and using gentle, natural skincare can help.✦Remember that mood swings are temporary.✦Enjoy growing your baby day by day.✦Darkening of the genital area is also a sign of 9 weeks of pregnancy.✦Your vaginal discharge may increase.✦If the discharge is yellow, smells bad or itches, tell your doctor.✦Keep eating protein regularly at this stage.✦Your calcium needs are also high now.✦Aim for 1,000–1,500 mg of calcium a day from food.✦If you can't drink milk, have cheese, yogurt or kefir.✦Avoid junk food, fast food and sugary foods.✦Satisfy your sweet tooth with fruit and naturally dried fruit.✦Well-washed salads and lightly cooked vegetables are great sources of vitamin C.✦When buying packaged food, including bread, read labels carefully and limit products with many additives and preservatives.✦Choose fresh, natural foods as much as possible.
mother.63: ✦This week some mothers-to-be may have a small amount of vaginal bleeding.✦It may not be anything bad, but you should still tell your doctor.
mother.64: ✦Your uterus is now the size of a grapefruit – twice its size before pregnancy.✦If this is your first baby, your belly probably isn't showing yet.✦You're probably feeling very tired.
mother.65: ✦At your next prenatal check-up, you may hear your baby's fast heartbeat with a Doppler.✦Your usual clothes may be getting tight; your breasts in particular may no longer fit your bra.✦This might be the week to start wearing maternity clothes.
mother.66: ✦Your belly keeps growing from both bloating and slight weight gain.✦Comfortable clothes with elastic waistbands will make your day easier.✦Depending on how sporty you are, you can do many activities.✦Swimming and walking are ideal choices throughout pregnancy.
mother.67: ✦Exercise is good for your stamina, muscles and strength.✦These help you carry the weight you gain, cope with physical stress and lose weight more easily after birth.
mother.68: ✦Iron, food for the brain, is one of the most important nutrients in a healthy pregnancy diet.✦Iron carries oxygen in your blood.✦Your baby needs iron for cognitive development.

mother.71: ✦This week your uterus is about the size of a medium grapefruit.✦Your doctor can feel its size by pressing gently on your belly just above the pubic bone.

mother.74: ✦Signs at this stage may include headaches, decreased or increased sex drive, sleep problems and skin issues such as stretch marks.

mother.77: ✦Since iron supplements can cause constipation, eat plenty of vegetables and salads.✦Don't rely only on supplements – try to eat foods like eggs, meat and spinach in a balanced way every day.✦Take your iron supplement a few hours before or after calcium-rich foods.✦Otherwise less iron is absorbed.

mother.79: ✦You're almost at the end of this month of pregnancy.✦This week your uterus is the size of a large grapefruit.✦As your uterus grows, it's normal to feel occasional aches in your sides.

mother.82: ✦If you didn't start last week, you may need to start iron supplements at 12 weeks – ask your doctor. Otherwise you may become anaemic, which can make you feel weak. Iron supplements also help protect against heavy bleeding at birth.

mother.94: ✦Although you feel much better than at first, you may still feel exhausted now and then.✦Your blood pressure may drop.✦Constipation may continue.

mother.119: ✦This week your baby's mammary glands and nipples are forming.✦In baby girls, millions of eggs keep forming in the ovaries.✦By birth this number will drop to about one to two million.✦In baby boys, the prostate will start forming next week.✦The eyes are moving into place and moving around, but the baby can't open the eyelids yet.

mother.127: ✦You may feel tired and low on energy.✦This common symptom is mostly due to hormonal changes and your heart working harder.✦Your circulatory system is going through big changes, and it's normal for your blood pressure to be lower than usual during this period.
mother.128: ✦If you haven't had it yet, your doctor may suggest the triple or quadruple screening test, recommended between weeks 16 and 20.✦These may not be needed if no risk was found in the first-trimester screening.✦Even with normal early results, factors like the mother's age or a family history of genetic conditions may make these tests advisable.✦Along with the scan, the baby's main organs, body systems, head and spine, brain, placenta position, amniotic fluid volume, heartbeat, blood vessels and sex are checked.✦The quadruple test is more comprehensive than the triple test.✦Doctors today usually prefer the quadruple test for that reason.✦If these tests show a risk, the doctor may suggest amniocentesis or other tests.

mother.133: ✦You may notice redness on your palms.✦This is due to extra estrogen and nothing to worry about.✦Some areas of your skin may darken.✦This is due to a temporary increase in pigment.✦If the darkening is on your lips, cheeks and forehead, it's called 'the mask of pregnancy' (melasma).✦You may also notice darkening on your nipples, dimples and scars, arms and vulva.✦The dark line running from your belly button down is known as the 'linea nigra'.✦These darker areas fade after birth.
mother.134: ✦At this stage you may get leg cramps when lying down.✦In some cases they're caused by a lack of certain minerals.✦Increasing your calcium intake can ease cramps.✦Salt your food to taste, but avoid too much salt.✦It can raise blood pressure.✦Cramps can also happen if you don't drink enough or sit too much.

mother.136: ✦If everything is fine, there's no harm in planning a holiday.✦A holiday is always good for couples, during pregnancy too.✦But keep a few things in mind when travelling: – Talk to your doctor before long trips. – When travelling by car, stop every 2 hours.✦During breaks, walk around or stretch your legs.
mother.137: ✦Pay attention to your iron levels at this stage.✦You can get iron, important for your blood, from a balanced diet.✦Get checked regularly to reduce the risk of anaemia.✦Your iron levels may be affected by other things you consume.✦Calcium and the phenolic compounds in tea and coffee can reduce iron absorption.
mother.138: ✦Before and during travel, avoid foods that upset your stomach.✦Don't overeat.✦Keep snacks like roasted chickpeas, dried fruit, raw hazelnuts, walnuts and almonds with you to balance your blood sugar and settle your stomach.

mother.254: ✦This week you're more comfortable in some ways.✦You may feel constantly hot and tired.✦That's because your body is working extra hard.✦The more blood your body circulates to nourish you and your baby, the more calories you burn.✦And this extra energy use raises your body temperature.
mother.255: ✦If you find yourself cleaning like mad, your nesting instinct has kicked in.✦It's an instinct that prepares you for birth.✦Not every woman feels it, and it's harmless as long as you don't move heavy furniture.✦Never lift heavy things, because your ligaments are softened by pregnancy.✦So your risk of twisting an ankle or hurting your back is very high.✦Ask for help when you need it.
mother.256: ✦If you want to clean, avoid harsh chemicals like bleach.✦If you have a cat, don't clean the litter box yourself, to avoid the risk of infection.✦Braxton Hicks contractions are now more frequent and stronger.
mother.257: ✦Your vaginal discharge may have increased.✦If you see a small amount of blood in your underwear or in the toilet, labour may be only a few days away.✦If you have heavy bleeding, call your doctor immediately.
mother.258: ✦Sleeping may feel harder than ever now.✦If possible, don't tire yourself out during the day.✦Keep tracking your baby's movements and call your doctor if you notice a decrease.
mother.259: ✦With birth possible any day, if you're having a boy, you may want to think about whether you plan circumcision.✦Some parents prefer to have it done soon after birth.✦Talking to your doctor about it will help you decide.
mother.260: ✦For most women the next few weeks are a waiting game.✦Use this time for your baby's room or jobs you won't have time for for a while after the birth.
mother.261: ✦Your baby is almost here; you can pack your hospital bag now.✦Besides personal and practical items, it helps to bring nutritious snacks in case you need an energy boost during labour.✦You won't want to eat much, but a bite or two of something nutritious can help you keep going.✦Pack different foods; you won't know what you'll want or be able to tolerate until the time comes.
mother.262: ✦You may find it harder and harder to sleep comfortably, especially at night.✦Rest often during the day and put your feet up. Nap, read and spend time with your partner while you can.

mother.266: ✦From this week, keep in mind that labour could start at any moment.✦The key feature of real labour pains is that they come at regular intervals.✦They come on average 3 times in 10 minutes, each lasting about 50 seconds.✦They don't go away with rest and get stronger over time.✦Generally about 75% of births happen between weeks 38 and 42.✦In about 5% of mothers-to-be, labour doesn't start even after 42 weeks.✦The remaining 20% give birth before week 38.
mother.267: ✦By 38 weeks most of the downy lanugo covering your baby's body has gone.✦The cheese-like vernix caseosa has mostly gone too (some may remain at birth).✦Your baby swallows both and keeps them in the intestines.✦They'll form the black stool passed in your baby's first bowel movements.✦This substance is called meconium.
mother.268: ✦Here are the signs of labour this week.✦More frequent false contractions (Braxton Hicks).✦A stronger nesting instinct (bursts of energy, e.g. cleaning and tidying the house non-stop).✦Regular contractions starting, every 10 or 15 minutes.✦Regular contractions lasting longer.✦Contractions becoming more frequent and intense.✦Contractions getting stronger when you walk or lie down.✦Period-like pain in your back and lower belly.✦Diarrhoea.✦Blood-tinged mucus as the cervix softens and the mucus plug comes away (often called a 'show').✦Needing the toilet often.✦A small or large gush of amniotic fluid (waters breaking).
mother.269: ✦If you have varicose veins, they may be more noticeable now.✦That's because progesterone relaxes your blood vessels.✦Your legs are also carrying more weight and more blood is circulating in your body.
mother.270: ✦Right now you're focused on the birth and welcoming your baby, but soon you'll need to focus on breastfeeding.✦Your breast milk – with carbohydrates, proteins, fats (including long-chain fatty acids), prebiotics, vitamins, antibodies and nucleotides – will nourish your baby and adapt to their changing needs as they grow, supporting their development.
mother.271: ✦You could give birth any moment now, so watch for signs of labour.✦These include your waters breaking, diarrhoea and nausea, a burst of energy, the mucus plug coming away and slightly bloody vaginal discharge.✦If you see blood in your discharge, labour may be 1–2 days away.✦But this isn't certain, so don't fixate on that timing.
mother.272: ✦At this stage you probably feel so uncomfortable that you may think you never want to be pregnant again.✦But we suggest waiting until you hold your baby before making that decision.
mother.273: ✦As a mother-to-be at this point, you may feel excited, distracted, anxious or even scared.✦You may be tense and overly sensitive.✦You may notice you're impatient and restless.✦All these emotional swings are completely normal.✦Go easy on yourself, relax and remember it will all be over very soon.
mother.274: ✦You probably feel huge right now.✦Your uterus now fills your pelvis and most of your belly, and there's no room left to grow.✦So it sits under your ribs, and measurements hardly change from week to week.
mother.275: ✦In the last month of pregnancy, nutrition is as important as ever.✦Keep eating a healthy, balanced diet and try not to gain much weight in the final week.✦Apart from your daily exercises, avoid activities that tire you.✦Travel isn't recommended in the final weeks of pregnancy.✦If you need to travel, talk to your doctor first.✦Take showers sitting down or with someone nearby.
mother.276: ✦Some women prefer not to use medication for pain relief during labour.✦They choose to give birth as naturally as possible using different positions, massage, hypnotherapy, and breathing and relaxation techniques.✦These methods are usually taught in birth preparation classes.✦In the final weeks of pregnancy, relaxation techniques can help you stay calm.

mother.280: ✦Newborns don't have as much blood on their skin as people think.✦For skin-to-skin contact after birth, the baby can be gently wiped with a towel and placed on the mother's chest.✦Delaying cord clamping by about a minute helps the baby part calmly from something familiar and helps prevent anaemia.✦Being placed on the mother right after birth lets the baby calm down to the sound of the mother's heartbeat.✦In recent years this has become common practice, recognising that before bathing or vaccines, the baby needs nothing more than the mother's arms.✦You can ask your doctor during pregnancy for skin-to-skin contact, now offered in many hospitals.✦It's very valuable for the baby to stay with the mother during and after the Apgar test.✦If there's no emergency, the baby should stay with the mother for the first 45 minutes to 1 hour.✦This way the baby feels safe, soothed by the parents' familiar voices and the feeling of being held (a natural incubator effect).✦Meeting this need for safety right after birth is said to help babies be calmer, including in infancy, and to trust life.✦If you request these practices in advance, you won't be disappointed after the birth.
